summary: Replaced the replay-completion account with the boundary-pinned version citing four receipts. Receipt 8a710c75d1814aafad5d24b536998539 places the bound exactly: at MaxAppendEntries 16 the prefix ending at staged index 2049 holds 2048 tuple-producing entries, i.e. 128 delivered batches (event 31), and NewRaft returned in 0ms (event 32, comparison holds), while the prefix ending at 2050 holds 2049 tuples, i.e. 129 delivered batches (event 34), and NewRaft did not return within 8000ms (witness event 35, three stack mentions naming the replay frames). The rationale now states the bound in delivered batches (128 x MaxAppendEntries, 8192 tuples at the default 64) and notes that the entry-based figure for the returning case also reads 129, so index-range counts are upper bounds; knowledge is cited at revision 2. Five knowledge uses, six counterevidence items (including that the delivered-tuple count is a harness-side derivation, that default-cadence reachability is still unmeasured, and the deliberate extra stop in the availability case) and four limitations. The three gaps opened by the knowledge correction could not be answered in this interpretation because they do not belong to its experiment lineage; that answer is the next step, and no new probe was submitted this turn.
